A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support comparison, including alignment of reorganized and renamed material.

before.justification: v1 contains algorithms, mathematical constructions, learning guarantees, and proofs, but no original experimental, simulation, or data-analysis results, including in its appendices.

after.justification: v2 remains theoretical throughout. Its additional comparisons concern analytical convergence rates, not original empirical evaluations.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 generalizes support-membership voting to maximizing weighted reward values, with updates depending on prediction and demonstration reward gaps. This enables general bounded rewards with suboptimal demonstrators, beyond v1's indicator-based updates. The optimal binary special case and greedy pass@k procedure are retained.

E1.justification: Neither version actually trains or evaluates on datasets or benchmarks. The broader theoretical reward and demonstrator assumptions do not constitute added empirical task coverage.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates experimental baselines. v2's comparisons with Syed and Schapire and Moulin et al. are analytical comparisons, assessed under T1 and R1.

E3.justification: Neither version reports experimental splits, preprocessing, training budgets, or testing protocols. Revised theoretical assumptions and sample-complexity formulas are not experimental setting changes.

E4.justification: Neither version contains empirical ablations, robustness tests, or error studies. The counterexamples and lower-bound constructions are theoretical analyses.

E5.justification: Neither reports repeated runs, seeds, empirical confidence intervals, or significance tests. Changes to high-probability mathematical guarantees belong to T1.

E6.justification: There are no empirical result entries in either version. The changed regret and sample-complexity bounds are theoretical results assessed under T1.

T1.justification: v2 replaces v1's fixed-factor suboptimal-demonstrator loss guarantees with general-reward regret and optimistic excess-value bounds in Theorems 5–6. It expands Proposition 1 and revises concentration arguments, removing log-log sample-size terms from reported optimal-demonstrator and pass@k bounds. The new proofs contain local errors: Appendix D.1 overstates a logarithmic inequality's gamma range, D.2 incorrectly simplifies a coefficient, and E.2 introduces an extra eta factor.

C1.justification: The central contribution expands from learning primarily from optimal demonstrations to matching arbitrary demonstrators' value under bounded rewards with optimistic rates. The abstract also qualifies the novelty claim through explicit similarity to Syed and Schapire, emphasizing rate and online-processing distinctions. Adaptive optimal demonstrations were already covered in v1.

C2.justification: v2 addresses v1 Section 6's open general-reward limitation and adds a substantive explanation of iterative reward discrimination and planning, distinguishing it from cloning and reward recovery. It newly discusses deterministic-transition MDP applicability and the unresolved suboptimal-demonstrator pass@k extension. Continuous-class and computational-tractability limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds guidance that action maximization may be solved to 1/m accuracy when an exact maximizer is unavailable, and specifies a gamma schedule using sample size, confidence, and demonstrator suboptimality. These extend v1's technical prescriptions without adding an implemented system or empirical reproducibility package.

R1.justification: New Section 5 develops a detailed correspondence with Syed and Schapire (2007) and discusses Moulin et al. (2025). Section 7 situates the method within reward-hedging apprenticeship approaches, including Swamy et al. This substantially revises contribution positioning; the earlier Kleinberg–Mullainathan comparison is removed.

P1.justification: The introduction, definitions, algorithm narrative, and interpretation sections are extensively rewritten around reward values. Former separate extensions are integrated into Section 4, pass@k moves to Section 6 and Appendix E, and properness discussion moves into Appendix D.3. Appendix C.2 also acquires a duplicated proof of Theorem 2.

P2.justification: Table 1 is expanded with rate formulas and explanatory shading; v2 adds Table 2 and an unnumbered comparison of apprenticeship approaches. Figures 1–2 receive revised descriptions or labels, and online-to-batch pseudocode is consolidated. The overall visual format remains similar.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens the treatment of the important limitation explicitly left open in v1: competing with suboptimal demonstrators under general bounded rewards. Its revised algorithm and convergence analysis, together with much clearer attribution and technical comparison to prior apprenticeship methods, are substantial quality gains. The new proofs still require local range and constant-factor corrections, and a duplicated proof reduces polish, but these shortcomings do not outweigh the broader theoretical treatment and improved research positioning.
